paragraphs.title: Abram Returns to the Land and Builds an Altar

easy.question: Where did Abram come from at the beginning of the passage?
easy.explanation: Verse 1 says, “Abram went up out of Egypt.”

easy.question: Who went with Abram?
answers: His wife, his possessions, and Lot
easy.explanation: The verse says that his wife, everything he had, and Lot went with him.

easy.question: What was Abram very wealthy in?
easy.explanation: Verse 2 says Abram was very rich in cattle, silver, and gold.

medium.question: Where did Abram go from the Negev?
medium.explanation: Verse 3 says Abram traveled from the Negev to Bethel.

medium.question: What did Abram do at the place of the altar?
answers: Called on the name of the Lord
medium.explanation: Verse 4 says that Abram called on the name of the Lord there.

medium.question: In the phrase “he went on his journeys from the south even to Bethel,” what does “journeys” mean?
answers: Places where he sold his possessions
medium.explanation: The context describes Abram traveling from the Negev to Bethel, so “journeys” means his travels and stopping places.

challenge.question: What can we infer from the text emphasizing that Abram was “very rich”?
answers: He had many possessions and herds
challenge.explanation: The verse explains this wealth by mentioning his livestock, silver, and gold.

challenge.question: Where was Abram’s tent at first?
challenge.explanation: Verse 3 says that his tent had initially been between Bethel and Hai.

challenge.question: What is the connection between verses 3 and 4?
answers: Abram left the altar and never returned
Abram went to Egypt and built an altar there
Abram returned to the place of his first altar and called on the name of the Lord
challenge.explanation: Verse 3 describes his return to Bethel, and verse 4 says he came to the place of the altar and called on the Lord.

questions.question: What can we infer from the text emphasizing that Abram was “very rich”?
answers: He had many possessions and herds
questions.explanation: The verse explains this wealth by mentioning his livestock, silver, and gold.

questions.question: Where was Abram’s tent at first?
questions.explanation: Verse 3 says that his tent had initially been between Bethel and Hai.

questions.question: What is the connection between verses 3 and 4?
answers: Abram left the altar and never returned
Abram went to Egypt and built an altar there
Abram returned to the place of his first altar and called on the name of the Lord
questions.explanation: Verse 3 describes his return to Bethel, and verse 4 says he came to the place of the altar and called on the Lord.

easy.question: Who had flocks, herds, and tents?
easy.explanation: The verse says that Lot, who traveled with Abram, also had flocks, herds, and tents.

easy.question: Between whom was there a dispute?
answers: Between Abram’s herdsmen and Lot’s herdsmen
easy.explanation: The verse says there was strife between Abram’s herdsmen and Lot’s herdsmen.

easy.question: What was so great that Abram and Lot could not dwell together?
easy.explanation: Their possessions were so great that the land could not support them both.

medium.question: Why could Abram and Lot not dwell together?
answers: Their possessions were great, and the land could not support them
medium.explanation: Their great wealth left insufficient room for both men and their livestock.

medium.question: In the phrase “the land was not able to bear them,” what does “bear” mean?
medium.explanation: Here, “bear” means that the land could not contain or support all their possessions and livestock.

medium.question: What is the correct order of events in these verses?
answers: The dispute, their great wealth, and then Lot’s departure
Leaving the land, the dispute, and then buying cattle
Great wealth, lack of space, and then a dispute between the herdsmen
medium.explanation: First the text describes their great possessions, then the lack of room, and finally the dispute between the herdsmen.

challenge.question: What can we infer from the mention of Lot’s flocks, herds, and tents?
answers: Lot had great wealth and managed a nomadic camp
Lot lived permanently in a city
Lot was engaged only in trade
challenge.explanation: Flocks, herds, and tents indicate great wealth and a mobile way of life.

challenge.question: Why is the mention of the Canaanites and Perizzites at the end of the verse significant?
answers: It proves that they settled the dispute
It emphasizes that the land was already inhabited and its resources were limited
It teaches that they were Abram’s herdsmen
challenge.explanation: The verse notes that the Canaanites and Perizzites lived in the land, so it was not completely empty.

challenge.question: What can we understand from the fact that the dispute was between the herdsmen, rather than Abram and Lot themselves?
answers: Abram and Lot did not know each other
The herdsmen were unrelated to their possessions
The tension concerned managing the livestock and pasture, while Abram and Lot’s relationship continued
challenge.explanation: The verse attributes the dispute to the herdsmen, describing a practical conflict over livestock rather than necessarily a personal break between Abram and Lot.

questions.question: What can we infer from the mention of Lot’s flocks, herds, and tents?
answers: Lot had great wealth and managed a nomadic camp
Lot lived permanently in a city
Lot was engaged only in trade
questions.explanation: Flocks, herds, and tents indicate great wealth and a mobile way of life.

answers: Abram and Lot did not know each other

questions.explanation: The verse attributes the dispute to the herdsmen, describing a practical conflict over livestock rather than necessarily a personal break between Abram and Lot.

easy.question: To whom did Abram speak?
easy.explanation: The verse begins, “Abram said unto Lot.”

easy.question: What did Abram ask them to avoid?
easy.explanation: Abram said, “Let there be no strife, I pray thee, between me and thee.”

easy.question: Who were the people Abram described by saying, “We be brethren”?
easy.explanation: Abram spoke to Lot and emphasized their close family relationship.

medium.question: Why did Abram suggest separating from Lot?
answers: To prevent a dispute between the herdsmen
Because he no longer wanted to see Lot
Because he wanted to leave the land
medium.explanation: Abram wanted to prevent the conflict that had arisen between his herdsmen and Lot’s.

medium.question: In the phrase “separate thyself, I pray thee, from me,” what does “separate” mean?
answers: Move away or part from me
medium.explanation: In the context of choosing different regions, “separate” means to move away and live apart.

medium.question: What did Abram offer Lot after suggesting that they separate?
answers: That Lot choose which direction to take
medium.explanation: Abram told Lot to choose whether to go left or right, and he would go in the opposite direction.

challenge.question: What does the phrase “We be brethren” mean in the context of Abram and Lot?
answers: They were brothers with the same father
challenge.explanation: Lot was a member of Abram’s family, so Abram emphasized their family bond, even though they were not actual brothers.

challenge.question: What quality of Abram is shown by letting Lot choose first?
answers: Generosity and a desire for peace
challenge.explanation: Abram gave up the first choice in order to prevent conflict and preserve his relationship with Lot.

challenge.question: What can we infer from the statement, “If thou wilt take the left hand, then I will go to the right”?
answers: Abram did not know where left and right were
Abram would choose the direction opposite to Lot
challenge.explanation: Abram offered to go in the opposite direction from Lot so they would not compete for the same area.

questions.question: What does the phrase “We be brethren” mean in the context of Abram and Lot?
answers: They were brothers with the same father
questions.explanation: Lot was a member of Abram’s family, so Abram emphasized their family bond, even though they were not actual brothers.

questions.question: What quality of Abram is shown by letting Lot choose first?
answers: Generosity and a desire for peace
questions.explanation: Abram gave up the first choice in order to prevent conflict and preserve his relationship with Lot.

questions.question: What can we infer from the statement, “If thou wilt take the left hand, then I will go to the right”?
answers: Abram did not know where left and right were
Abram would choose the direction opposite to Lot
questions.explanation: Abram offered to go in the opposite direction from Lot so they would not compete for the same area.

paragraphs.title: Lot Chooses the Plain of Jordan and Moves Toward Sodom

easy.question: What did Lot see when he lifted up his eyes?
easy.explanation: The verse says that Lot saw all the plain of Jordan.

easy.question: What did Lot choose?
easy.explanation: The verse says, “Lot chose him all the plain of Jordan.”

easy.question: Where did Abram dwell?
answers: In the cities of the plain
easy.explanation: The verse says, “Abram dwelled in the land of Canaan.”

medium.question: Why did the plain of Jordan appeal to Lot?
answers: It was well watered and appeared fertile
Abram asked him to choose it
medium.explanation: Lot saw that the plain was well watered, so it looked like the garden of the Lord and the land of Egypt.

medium.question: What happened after Lot chose the plain of Jordan?
answers: Lot journeyed east, and Abram and Lot separated
medium.explanation: After Lot chose the plain, he journeyed east, and the two men separated.

medium.question: In the phrase “it was well watered every where,” what does “well watered” mean?
medium.explanation: “Well watered” describes a place with plentiful water; therefore the plain appeared fertile like a garden.

challenge.question: What can we infer was Lot’s main consideration in choosing the area?
answers: He focused mainly on its fertility and abundant water
He chose it because of the holiness of its inhabitants
He chose it at Abram’s instruction
challenge.explanation: Lot focused on the plain’s abundant water and fertile appearance, even though the people of Sodom were wicked and sinful.

challenge.question: What was the difference between where Abram and Lot lived after they separated?
answers: They both lived in the cities of the plain
Abram lived in Canaan, while Lot lived in the cities of the plain
Abram lived in Sodom, while Lot lived in Canaan
challenge.explanation: The verses state that Abram remained in Canaan, while Lot lived in the cities of the plain.

challenge.question: What does the phrase “before the Lord destroyed Sodom and Gomorrah” teach?
answers: Sodom had already been destroyed when Lot chose
The destruction caused the plain to be well watered
The plain looked fertile at the time of the choice, before its future destruction
challenge.explanation: The phrase indicates that the plain’s fertile condition is being described before the Lord destroyed Sodom and Gomorrah.

questions.question: What can we infer was Lot’s main consideration in choosing the area?
answers: He focused mainly on its fertility and abundant water
He chose it because of the holiness of its inhabitants
He chose it at Abram’s instruction
questions.explanation: Lot focused on the plain’s abundant water and fertile appearance, even though the people of Sodom were wicked and sinful.

questions.question: What was the difference between where Abram and Lot lived after they separated?
answers: They both lived in the cities of the plain
Abram lived in Canaan, while Lot lived in the cities of the plain
Abram lived in Sodom, while Lot lived in Canaan
questions.explanation: The verses state that Abram remained in Canaan, while Lot lived in the cities of the plain.

questions.question: What does the phrase “before the Lord destroyed Sodom and Gomorrah” teach?
answers: Sodom had already been destroyed when Lot chose
The destruction caused the plain to be well watered
The plain looked fertile at the time of the choice, before its future destruction
questions.explanation: The phrase indicates that the plain’s fertile condition is being described before the Lord destroyed Sodom and Gomorrah.

paragraphs.title: The Lord Promises Abram the Land and Descendants

easy.question: To whom did the Lord say to lift up his eyes and look at the land?
easy.explanation: The Lord spoke to Abram and told him to lift up his eyes and look at the land.

easy.question: In which directions was Abram told to look?
easy.explanation: The verse names all four directions: north, south, east, and west.

easy.question: What was Abram’s seed compared to?
easy.explanation: The Lord said that Abram’s seed would be like the dust of the earth, which cannot be numbered.

medium.question: What happened before the Lord spoke to Abram?
medium.explanation: The verse begins, “after that Lot was separated from him,” so the separation came first.

medium.question: What is the connection between seeing the land and the promise to Abram?
answers: The land he saw would be given to him and his seed
The land was intended only for Lot
Abram was required to leave the land
medium.explanation: The Lord said that all the land Abram saw would be given to him and his seed.

medium.question: In the phrase “walk through the land in the length of it and in the breadth of it,” what does “length” refer to?
medium.explanation: “Length” refers to traveling along the length of the land; together with “breadth,” it describes its full extent.

challenge.question: According to these verses, to whom was the land promised?
answers: Only to Abram during his lifetime
To Abram and his seed forever
Only to his seed after his death
challenge.explanation: The verse says, “To thee will I give it, and to thy seed for ever,” including both Abram and his descendants.

challenge.question: What can we infer from the command for Abram to walk through the land in its length and breadth?
answers: He was to become familiar with and travel throughout the land
He was to remain in one place
He was to search for another land
challenge.explanation: Mentioning the land’s length and breadth suggests traveling through and becoming familiar with its entire extent.

challenge.question: What does the image of the dust of the earth emphasize about Abram’s seed?
answers: They would be impossible to count
They would live only in the wilderness
They would be made of dust
challenge.explanation: The verse explains that just as the dust cannot be counted, Abram’s seed would also be beyond counting.

questions.question: According to these verses, to whom was the land promised?
answers: Only to Abram during his lifetime
To Abram and his seed forever
Only to his seed after his death
questions.explanation: The verse says, “To thee will I give it, and to thy seed for ever,” including both Abram and his descendants.

questions.question: What can we infer from the command for Abram to walk through the land in its length and breadth?
answers: He was to become familiar with and travel throughout the land
He was to remain in one place
He was to search for another land
questions.explanation: Mentioning the land’s length and breadth suggests traveling through and becoming familiar with its entire extent.

questions.question: What does the image of the dust of the earth emphasize about Abram’s seed?
answers: They would be impossible to count
They would live only in the wilderness
They would be made of dust
questions.explanation: The verse explains that just as the dust cannot be counted, Abram’s seed would also be beyond counting.

paragraphs.title: Abram Settles in Hebron and Builds an Altar

easy.question: Who settled by the plain of Mamre?
easy.explanation: The verse says that Abram moved his tent, came, and dwelled by the plain of Mamre.

easy.question: Where was the plain of Mamre?
easy.explanation: The verse says that Mamre was in Hebron.

easy.question: What did Abram build there?
easy.explanation: Abram built an altar there unto the Lord.

medium.question: What did Abram do after coming to and dwelling by the plain of Mamre?
medium.explanation: After settling there, Abram built an altar to the Lord.

medium.question: In the phrase “the plain of Mamre, which is in Hebron,” what does “plain” refer to?
answers: An open area or level region
medium.explanation: Here, “plain” refers to the open region where Abram pitched his tent and lived.

medium.question: What can we understand from the fact that Abram built an altar to the Lord where he lived?
answers: He wanted to worship and give thanks to the Lord
He wanted to build a city
medium.explanation: An altar to the Lord was connected with worship, thanksgiving, and faith.

challenge.question: Which phrase shows that Mamre is the place’s name and Hebron identifies the area where it was located?
challenge.explanation: The phrase “which is in Hebron” explains that the plain of Mamre was located in Hebron.

challenge.question: What does the word “there” indicate in the sentence “and built there an altar”?
answers: The altar was built where Abram had settled
The altar was built in another land
The altar was built before Abram arrived
challenge.explanation: “There” refers back to the place just mentioned—the plain of Mamre in Hebron.

challenge.question: Which sequence of events matches the verse?
answers: Abram built an altar, then came, and finally settled
Abram settled in Hebron, then left, and finally built an altar
Abram moved his tent, came and settled, and then built an altar
challenge.explanation: The verse presents the events in this order: Abram moved his tent, came and settled, and then built an altar.

questions.question: Which phrase shows that Mamre is the place’s name and Hebron identifies the area where it was located?
questions.explanation: The phrase “which is in Hebron” explains that the plain of Mamre was located in Hebron.

questions.question: What does the word “there” indicate in the sentence “and built there an altar”?
answers: The altar was built where Abram had settled
The altar was built in another land
The altar was built before Abram arrived
questions.explanation: “There” refers back to the place just mentioned—the plain of Mamre in Hebron.

questions.question: Which sequence of events matches the verse?
answers: Abram built an altar, then came, and finally settled
Abram settled in Hebron, then left, and finally built an altar
Abram moved his tent, came and settled, and then built an altar
questions.explanation: The verse presents the events in this order: Abram moved his tent, came and settled, and then built an altar.
